findings.rule: robustness: no traceback, no regression (crash on malformed config)
findings.evidence: resolve_review_identity now loads .specs/semantic/config.yaml on every path, including when --model is given. load_semantic_config can raise ValueError (invalid YAML), UnicodeDecodeError (non-UTF-8) or IsADirectoryError/OSError, and none of these is turned into ReviewIdentityError. In lane.py:162 the call sits outside the old `except (OSError, ValueError)` at line 170. delivery_cmd._lane (lines 59/63), goal_delivery_lane (goal.py:30) and render_goal_command (goal_cli_actions.py:90) catch only DeliveryInputError or ReviewIdentityError. I ran CliRunner probes against the working tree and against an extracted HEAD tree with config `review_model: [unclosed`. `delivery lane --feature 001-export --model reviewer/v1 --json` gave exit 0 (full lane) at HEAD and gives an uncaught ValueError traceback (exit 1) with 093. `goal render spec-implement --flags --model=reviewer/v1` and `goal render spec-plan --flags --model=reviewer/v1` both rendered with exit 0 at HEAD and now raise a ValueError traceback. A non-UTF-8 config file or a directory at that path gives the same result (UnicodeDecodeError / IsADirectoryError tracebacks). `validate --progression` and `delivery revision open` still exit cleanly (BLOCKED / Error), except revision open on a directory, which tracebacks in both versions.
findings.correction: In resolve_review_identity, wrap load_semantic_config in `try/except (OSError, ValueError) as exc: raise ReviewIdentityError("review_config_invalid", f"{type(exc).__name__}: .specs/semantic/config.yaml") from exc`. UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, so it is covered. Every caller already maps ReviewIdentityError to a clean exit: lane/review exit 2, goal render exit 2, progression/revision exit 1, goal_delivery_lane full lane. Add parametrized tests for invalid YAML, non-UTF-8 and directory configs across lane (with and without --model), goal render (spec-plan and spec-implement) and progression.

findings.rule: fail-closed identity / review-protocol 'CLI refuses to save an unusable review-bearing goal'
findings.evidence: Only exact '', 'default' and 'unknown' are refused. `review_model: ' '` (or `--model ' '`) resolves to the model ' '. With that config, `goal render spec-plan --feature 001-export --json` exits 0 and binds reviewer_model ' '. Progression stays fail-closed (spec_review_model_mismatch:reviewer/v1!= ) and lane stays full, so nothing passes wrongly, but an unusable review-bearing goal is saved.
findings.correction: Normalize first: `resolved = resolved.strip()`, then refuse it when `not resolved or resolved.lower() in _UNNAMED` (or require a printable token without whitespace). Apply the same to configured_model candidates.

findings.rule: robustness: no traceback on malformed flag
findings.evidence: `budget.isdigit()` accepts Unicode digits such as '²', but `int('²')` raises ValueError. `goal render spec-plan --flags --review-max-chars=²` ends in an uncaught ValueError traceback. delivery/goal.py:27 has the same pattern. HEAD also tracebacks on this input, so this is not a regression.
findings.correction: Use `budget.isascii() and budget.isdigit()`, or `try: int(budget) except ValueError: raise ReviewIdentityError('review_max_chars_out_of_bounds', ...)`. In delivery/goal.py, refuse or flag an invalid explicit budget instead of silently falling back to the configured one.

findings.evidence: The error message embeds `budget!r` with no length limit. A 400-digit review_max_chars printed the whole value in lane, progression and goal render errors. Any long configured string would be echoed in full. There are no secrets in this field, but output size is unbounded.
findings.correction: Truncate the repr (for example `reprlib.repr(budget)`) or print only its type when it is not an int.

findings.evidence: configured_model returns the first non-empty string. With `review_reviewers: [default, real/m]` it returns 'default', which _UNNAMED then refuses (review_model_required), even though a valid second reviewer exists. This fails closed, but the result may surprise users.
findings.correction: Skip _UNNAMED placeholders inside configured_model, or document that the first entry must name a real model.

findings.evidence: The tests cover a missing or empty model, an int model, budgets that are out of bounds, bool, float or string, inclusive bounds, and goal render, progression, lane and revision open. They do not cover invalid YAML, a non-dict top level, a non-list review_reviewers, a whitespace-only model, a non-UTF-8 or unreadable config, or delivery review prepare/verify and pipeline next/update with an unresolved identity. My probes show these paths currently give clean exits (except the blocking case above), but no test pins that behavior.
findings.correction: Add parametrized cases for these configs at resolve_review_identity level and at least one CLI case each for lane --model, goal render --model and pipeline next.
